price_note: Digital teacher guide and student materials are free to download; the optional physical robot is sold separately.
source_site: YES - Youth Engineering Solutions (Museum of Science, Boston)
standards: Aligned to K-2 Computer Science standards (Data & Analysis; Algorithms & Programming) per publisher.
udl_rationale: action_expression: offers both a plugged (physical robot) and unplugged (peer-as-robot) pathway so students can show programming skill in the format that fits them; engagement: the real-world recycling/park cleanup story gives the coding task a concrete purpose
evidence: Students learn how to give instructions to a robot. They modify their programs to include repeating instructions to make it easy to tell the robot to do the same action several times.

title: Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set
description: A screen-free programmable robot mouse and maze set that lets K-2 students physically sequence directional coding cards to guide the mouse through a maze, building a tactile sense of algorithms before ever touching a keyboard.
subject: CS / STEM
materials: Code & Go Robot Mouse Activity Set (robot, maze grids/walls, coding cards) — physical kit sold separately
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to sequence directional coding cards to program a robot mouse through a maze.
Students will be able to debug a program by testing and revising the card sequence when the mouse takes a wrong turn.
price_note: Physical activity set must be purchased from Learning Resources; this page hosts a free accessible activity guide.
source_site: American Printing House for the Blind (APH) Tech — accessible guide for Learning Resources' Code & Go Robot Mouse
udl_rationale: action_expression: students physically place coding cards and watch the result immediately, a non-keyboard way to program; representation: directional arrow cards use symbols instead of text, accessible to pre-readers
evidence: Coding literally means the transformation of data into a form understandable by a computer-basically, telling a computer what you want it to do.

title: Thinking with KIBO: Introducing AI in Early Grades
description: A free 5-lesson curriculum that uses the screen-free KIBO robot to introduce early-elementary students to basic artificial-intelligence ideas, letting them snap together wooden coding blocks to test how a 'thinking' machine makes decisions.
subject: CS / STEM
materials: KIBO robot kit (sold separately); free printable curriculum guide
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to build a simple KIBO program using sequenced wooden blocks to represent a decision an AI system might make.
Students will be able to describe one way a computer/AI system 'senses,' 'thinks,' and 'acts' using their KIBO robot as an example.
price_note: The curriculum guide is a free download; using it fully requires a KIBO robot kit, sold separately.
udl_rationale: engagement: physically building and running a robot sustains attention better than a screen-based AI demo; action_expression: wooden block programming lets students test ideas by rearranging objects, not writing text
evidence: Early STEM education, where children learn at a young age about technology, computers, coding, and AI, is the key to giving children understanding and mastery of AI tools.

title: Barefoot Computing: Primary Computing Resources
description: A UK library of 80+ cross-curricular computing lesson plans for ages 5-11, including an Age 5-7 strand of short, often screen-free activities that teach algorithms, sequencing, and debugging alongside subjects like literacy and PE.
subject: CS / STEM
publisher: Barefoot Computing (BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT)
materials: Varies by lesson; many need no computer
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to describe a sequence of instructions as an algorithm.
Students will be able to spot and fix a mistake (debug) in a simple set of instructions.
price_note: Free with a teacher account registration.
standards: Aligned to the UK National Curriculum for Computing, Key Stage 1 (ages 5-7).
udl_rationale: representation: lessons cross-link computing ideas into literacy/PE so the same concept is met in more than one context; engagement: many activities are physical/unplugged, giving movement-based learners a way in
evidence: over 80 cross-curricular lesson plans and resources that bring computing to life, with or without a computer

title: Climate Change and Cars (K-2 Lesson)
description: A free K-2 lesson from TeachEngineering.org that uses video, guided worksheets, and a think-pair-share discussion to introduce how gas-powered cars affect climate, closing with a formative 'Making Sense' assessment worksheet.
subject: CS / STEM
materials: Printed worksheets; internet access for video; no special equipment
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to explain in simple terms how gas-powered cars contribute to climate change.
Students will be able to complete a 'Making Sense' assessment worksheet showing what they learned about cars and climate.
standards: NGSS-aligned (K-2 Engineering Design / Earth and Human Activity).
udl_rationale: representation: pairs video with a guided worksheet so the same content is delivered by ear and by print; engagement: think-pair-share discussion lets students process the topic verbally with a partner before writing
evidence: Understanding the negative impact gas-powered cars have on the environment empowers engineers to develop alternative modes of transportation.

title: Jack and the Beanstalk: Beanstalk Building
description: A free hands-on K-1 STEM activity from Arizona State University's outreach program where students use simple craft materials to build the tallest possible 'beanstalk,' then measure and compare results with classmates.
subject: CS / STEM
publisher: Arizona STEM Acceleration Project (ASAP), Arizona State University
materials: Simple craft/building materials (e.g., straws, tape, paper) and a measuring tool
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to construct a free-standing tower/structure using basic building materials.
Students will be able to measure their structure's height and compare it with a classmate's using nonstandard or standard units.
source_site: Arizona State University STEM Teachers (ASAP outreach)
udl_rationale: engagement: ties the build challenge to a familiar fairy tale so students have a story hook for the task; action_expression: students show learning by building and measuring a physical object rather than writing about it
evidence: Students build the tallest beanstalk they can with the provided materials. They then measure it and compare their beanstalk heights.

title: TeachEngineering: K-2 STEM Curriculum Search
description: A free, searchable library of NGSS-aligned K-12 STEM lessons and activities from the University of Colorado Boulder; filtering to the K-2 grade band surfaces dozens of vetted, hands-on engineering-design lessons teachers can browse and download.
subject: CS / STEM
publisher: TeachEngineering (University of Colorado Boulder and partner institutions, NSF-funded)
materials: Varies by lesson
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to complete the steps of the engineering design process (ask, imagine, plan, create, improve) in a chosen K-2 lesson.
Students will be able to test a simple prototype and redesign it based on the results.
standards: NGSS Engineering Design; filterable by state and Common Core standards.
udl_rationale: engagement: topic filters (space, robotics, environment, etc.) let teachers match a lesson to what their class is curious about; representation: each lesson bundles video, images, and text so teachers can pick the best format for their students
evidence: Free, standards-aligned STEM curriculum for K-12. A collaboration of the University of Colorado Boulder and partner institutions, funded by the National Science Foundation.

title: 5 African Safari Animals Yoga Poses for Kids
description: Children take an imaginary safari trip and hold five animal yoga poses in sequence: giraffe, zebra, ostrich, elephant, and a cheetah pose where they go onto all fours, extend one leg back and pretend to race. No mat or equipment needed, so it runs on a classroom carpet.
subject: PE / Health
materials: Open floor space; no props required
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to copy and hold five animal-inspired body shapes on cue
Students will be able to name five African safari animals and describe how each one moves
price_note: Pose instructions are free on the page; the site also sells printable yoga cards and books.
udl_rationale: engagement: an imaginary safari journey frames the poses as a story, which sustains attention for children who disengage from drill-style movement; action_expression: children show what they know with their bodies rather than with words, and poses can be simplified or held for shorter counts.
evidence: Pretend to be a racing cheetah.

title: Safari Theme Activities for Pre-K and Preschool
description: A teacher-built safari theme set that includes a two-word brain break: children run in place fast on 'Cheetah!' and freeze or move in slow motion on 'Turtle!'. The rest of the page adds safari art, literacy, math and science ideas built around the same animals.
subject: Science
materials: None for the movement game; other ideas use pattern blocks, cotton balls, cardboard tubes and printables
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to change speed of movement on a spoken cue
Students will be able to match safari animals to how fast or slow they move
price_note: Most ideas are free; some linked printables are sold on Teachers Pay Teachers.
udl_rationale: engagement: a fast/slow contrast game needs no setup and pulls in children who are losing focus mid-lesson; action_expression: the response is whole-body, so children who cannot yet answer verbally still participate fully.
evidence: When you say "Cheetah!", kids run in place super fast.

title: Ocean Animal Movements
description: Printed ocean animal cards are taped around the room, and children travel to each one and act out that animal: opening and closing like a clam, digging like a crab, jumping like a dolphin, singing like a humpback whale. It doubles as a room-scale gross motor circuit.
subject: PE / Health
materials: Free printable ocean animal action cards, cardstock, painter's tape
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to name eight ocean animals
Students will be able to act out a movement that matches each named ocean animal
license: Not stated on page; printable offered as a free download
udl_rationale: engagement: children move around the room instead of sitting, so the activity holds attention far longer than a picture book about the same animals; representation: each animal arrives as a picture, a spoken name and a movement at once, giving three routes to the same vocabulary.
evidence: When you get to a card, point to the picture, say the name of the ocean animal, read the action statement.

title: Move Like a Penguin
description: A movement bank of penguin actions children perform on call: waddling with feet together, flapping wings, sliding on the belly, huddling together for warmth, balancing an 'egg' on the feet, and diving for fish. Runs as Simon Says, a dice roll, or a card draw.
subject: PE / Health
materials: None required; optional movement cards or a large foam dice
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to balance on one foot and walk with feet together in a penguin waddle
Students will be able to describe two ways real penguins move in their icy habitat
udl_rationale: engagement: the teacher can pick two moves for a 60-second wiggle break or run the whole set as a lesson, matching the class's energy; action_expression: several moves target different skills (balancing, sliding, hopping), so a child who cannot hop can still slide or huddle.
evidence: Encourage children to get creative with their movements and have fun exploring the various ways penguins navigate their icy habitats!

title: Dinosaur Roll and Move Gross Motor Activity
description: Children take turns rolling a soft pocket cube loaded with dinosaur movement cards, then the whole group performs whatever came up — twisting like a T-Rex, stretching tall like a Brachiosaurus. Turn-taking around the cube is built into the game.
subject: PE / Health
materials: Soft pocket cube, free printable dinosaur movement cards, scissors, optional laminator
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to perform a movement that matches the dinosaur shown on the card
Students will be able to wait for their turn to roll the cube
udl_rationale: engagement: the random roll keeps the next move unknown, which sustains interest through repeated rounds; action_expression: children respond with large body movements and each card can be scaled down for a child with limited mobility.
evidence: Waiting for a turn is a very difficult for young children which helps them develop self-regulation skills.

title: Act Out the Life Cycle of a Butterfly
description: A no-materials creative movement sequence: children curl into balls as eggs, wiggle along the floor as hungry caterpillars, stand still with arms wrapped as a chrysalis, then spread their arms and fly as butterflies. The teacher narrates each stage as a cue.
subject: Science
materials: None; optional picture books about butterflies
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to act out the four stages of the butterfly life cycle in order
Students will be able to name the egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly stages
udl_rationale: engagement: acting out metamorphosis turns an abstract sequence into something children feel in their own bodies, which holds three-year-olds far better than a diagram; action_expression: sequence knowledge is demonstrated through movement, so pre-readers and children with limited expressive language can show mastery.
evidence: Start out as tiny eggs, rolled up in a ball on the floor!

title: Caterpillar and Butterfly Life Cycle Art Activity: Shape Caterpillars
description: Children glue pre-cut circles and rectangles onto green paper to build a caterpillar body, feet and antennae, then add details with markers. The finished caterpillars become pages in a small life cycle book covering egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly.
subject: Science
materials: Green construction paper, pre-cut circles and rectangles, squeeze-bottle glue, markers, crayons, binder rings
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to build a caterpillar using circle and rectangle shapes
Students will be able to order the four stages of the butterfly life cycle in a book
udl_rationale: representation: the life cycle is presented as a sequence of physical pages the child can turn and revisit, not a one-time verbal explanation; action_expression: children build and draw rather than write, and the pre-cut shapes remove the scissor barrier for children still developing hand strength.
evidence: Using glue from a squeeze bottle requires effort, which is a great way to sneak in some hand/arm strengthening!

title: Farm Animals - Music & Movement Lesson Plan
description: A full circle-time music session built on farm animals: a hello song with actions, parachute play, animal sound call-and-response, the Chicken Dance, high and low pitch with instruments, and acting out each animal to music before a goodbye song.
subject: Arts
materials: Parachute, music player, farm animal pictures, beach ball, percussion instruments (tambourines, shakers, bells)
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to make the sound and movement that matches each farm animal
Students will be able to tell the difference between a high and a low pitch
udl_rationale: engagement: the session cycles through parachute, singing, instruments and dance, so a child who tunes out of one format is re-engaged by the next within minutes; representation: each farm animal is delivered as a picture, a sound, a song lyric and a movement.
evidence: How fun it is to visit the farm! Don't you love farm animals?

title: From Seeds to Plants
description: A short PreK science lesson where the teacher shows a live plant and a handful of seeds, then leads children through what a seed needs - soil, water, sunshine - before they observe and discuss how a seed becomes a plant.
subject: Science
materials: Live plant, seeds, soil, water, sunlight
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to identify how seeds develop into plants
Students will be able to name what a seed needs in order to grow
price_note: The lesson text is readable free; Education.com also sells a premium membership for some downloads.
udl_rationale: representation: children handle real seeds and a real plant alongside the spoken explanation, which anchors an abstract process in something concrete; engagement: the lesson connects to a planting project children can tend over following days, giving the learning a visible payoff.
evidence: Tell students that today they will be learning how seeds grow and develop into plants with the help of soil, water, sunshine, and carbon dioxide.

title: Autumn Leaves Preschool Science
description: Children collect red and yellow autumn leaves, then press half of them under heavy books overnight and leave the rest in the open air. Over three days they compare the two groups by look, feel and smell, and record what changed.
subject: Science
materials: Fresh autumn leaves, heavy books, white paper, free printable observation chart
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to describe how a leaf changes over three days
Students will be able to compare two groups of leaves by texture and colour
license: Not stated on page; observation chart offered as a free download
udl_rationale: representation: children gather evidence through sight, touch and smell rather than through a single verbal explanation of what leaves do in autumn; engagement: the outdoor collection walk and the multi-day wait give children a stake in the result.
evidence: The crunch of dried leaves, the weight of heavy books, and the interesting results of the experiment all stack up to make this a fun fall activity.

title: Rain Cloud in a Jar
description: A four-step weather demonstration children run themselves: fill a clear jar with water, spray shaving cream on top for the cloud, then drip food colouring onto the foam and watch the colour sink through in streaks like falling rain.
subject: Science
materials: Clear glass jar, water, white shaving cream, liquid food colouring, dropper
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to explain that rain falls when a cloud holds too much water
Students will be able to predict and then describe what happens to the colour in the jar
udl_rationale: representation: an invisible process in the sky becomes a visible one in a jar, at the child's eye level; engagement: the dropper work gives every child a turn at the moment the rain appears, rather than watching the teacher demonstrate.
evidence: The food coloring is sinking through the shaving cream cloud, like real rain falls from the sky!

title: Geometry for Kids: Finding Shapes at the Playground
description: Children take a printable shape checklist out to the playground and hunt for circles, squares, rectangles and triangles in the climbing frames and equipment, photographing each find. The photos are then printed and stapled into a labelled shape book.
subject: Math
materials: Free printable shape hunt checklist, camera or phone, printer, paper, stapler
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to find and name circles, squares, rectangles and triangles in the real world
Students will be able to match a found object to the shape word on a checklist
udl_rationale: engagement: shape learning moves outdoors onto equipment children already love, which reaches learners who disengage from worksheet geometry; action_expression: children demonstrate shape knowledge by pointing, photographing and building a book instead of by writing.
evidence: As we walked around the playground we found circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles from different angles in the play structures.

title: Five Little Ducks Number Line Gross Motor Activity
description: Numbered duck cards are taped to the floor in order to make a walkable number line. Children hop, jump or step from duck to duck saying each number aloud. Numbers can be swapped out of order, or one removed, for children to spot what is missing.
subject: Math
materials: Free printable duck number cards, tape, optional laminator
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to count aloud from one to five while stepping along a number line
Students will be able to identify a missing number in a sequence
price_note: The printable is delivered through a free email sign-up.
udl_rationale: engagement: pairing counting with a familiar song and with hopping keeps children in the activity longer than counters at a table; action_expression: a child shows number order by moving their body along the line, which works before they can write numerals.
evidence: Counting is an important early math skill that's a precursor to learning number names and values.

title: ABC Cookies Preschool Alphabet Activity
description: A bakery dramatic play set-up for letter matching: paper plates are labelled with lowercase letters, and children lift foam uppercase letters with a spatula onto the matching plate, then serve the 'cookies' to dolls or classmates.
subject: ELA / Reading
materials: Small paper plates labelled with lowercase letters, foam alphabet letters, baking sheet, spatula, optional apron
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to match an uppercase letter to its lowercase partner
Students will be able to name the letters they serve during play
udl_rationale: engagement: embedding letter matching inside a bakery role-play gives a purpose children care about, unlike flashcard drill; action_expression: children handle, scoop and serve physical letters, so success does not depend on naming letters aloud.
evidence: Tinker loved matching the upper and lowercase letters as she served up a whole batch of ABC cookies.

title: A is for Apple: Building Letter-Recognition Fluency
description: Children hunt for hidden letter cards around the room, visit online alphabet games to find words starting with each letter, then draw a picture for every letter to build their own ABC book, which they read to a partner.
subject: ELA / Reading
materials: Hidden letter cards on cardstock, chart paper, index cards, computers with internet access, My ABC Book handout
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to recognise and name letters of the alphabet fluently
Students will be able to produce a word beginning with a given letter and illustrate it
standards: Common Core State Standards; NCTE/IRA National Standards for the English Language Arts
udl_rationale: representation: letters are met as physical cards, as online game targets and as drawings, so the same content reaches children through three channels; action_expression: children show mastery by searching, drawing and reading aloud rather than only by writing.
evidence: Becoming fluent in letter recognition helps children to become more familiar and at ease with the alphabet.

title: Calm Down Corner Printables and Ideas
description: A guide to setting up one quiet classroom corner with soft seating, a sensory bottle and free printable strategy cards, plus an 'I Can Calm Down' book children page through to pick a strategy such as deep breathing when they feel upset.
subject: SEL
materials: Free printable calm down strategy cards, 'I Can Calm Down' book, emotion picture-word cards, cushion or bean bag, sensory bottle
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to choose a calming strategy from the picture cards
Students will be able to name the feeling they are having using the emotion cards
price_note: Printables are free; the site also sells related packs on Teachers Pay Teachers.
license: Printables are for personal, non-commercial use only
udl_rationale: engagement: children choose their own strategy and their own timing, which builds self-regulation rather than relying on adult direction; representation: strategies appear as pictures plus words, so a pre-reader can use the cards independently.
evidence: Young children are still learning how to manage their emotions

title: Emotions Activity with Paper Plate Faces
description: Children paint paper plates as faces, then use velcro-backed eye and mouth shapes to swap expressions on and off. A named feeling or a short scenario is called out and children build the face that matches it.
subject: SEL
materials: Paper plates, acrylic paint and brushes, foam sheets or felt, velcro dots, popsicle sticks
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to build a face that matches a named feeling
Students will be able to name at least four feelings from their facial expressions
udl_rationale: representation: feelings are shown as changeable physical features rather than described in words, which makes the link between expression and emotion concrete; action_expression: a child answers by moving velcro pieces, so children with little expressive language can still show they understand.
evidence: Being aware of feelings and why they get them, can help them learn how to control their reactions to strong emotions in the future.

title: Chinese Dragon for the New Year
description: The class builds a wearable dragon head from a painted cardboard box with egg-carton eyes and yarn, then a line of children carries a blanket behind it as the body and parades through the school while classmates play instruments alongside.
subject: Social Studies
materials: Large cardboard box, paint and brushes, egg carton, yarn, glue, string, jewels, blanket, classroom instruments
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to explain what the dragon stands for in Lunar New Year celebrations
Students will be able to move together as one group to carry the dragon in a parade
price_note: The activity page is free; the source book is sold separately.
udl_rationale: engagement: a whole-class parade gives every child a visible role and ties a cultural celebration to something they build themselves; action_expression: children can take part by constructing, by carrying the dragon, or by playing an instrument, so there are three ways in.
evidence: The Chinese dragon is a symbol of strength, wisdom, health, and good luck.

title: We're Going on a Bear Hunt Early Years Activities
description: Eight classroom activities built on the story, including 'Mission Impossible: Bear Hunt', where children run an outdoor obstacle course and copy each movement as the teacher narrates - wading through long grass, trudging through mud, tiptoeing into the cave.
subject: ELA / Reading
materials: Outdoor or indoor space, cushions, fabric, sensory trays with water, mud, sand and grass; the picture book
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to retell the story in order by moving through matching obstacles
Students will be able to use positional words such as over, under and through
udl_rationale: engagement: the obstacle course makes story sequence something children move through rather than sit and listen to, which suits children who cannot hold still for a full read-aloud; action_expression: retelling is demonstrated physically, so children who are not yet talking in full sentences can still show they know the order.
evidence: Encourage the children to imitate their movements as you read the story aloud.

title: Moon Phases with Cookies
description: Students scrape the frosting inside Oreo-style sandwich cookies to sculpt each of the eight moon phases, then line the cookies up in order to model one full lunar cycle.
subject: Science
materials: 8 sandwich cookies per student or pair, popsicle stick or plastic scraper
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to name and sequence the eight phases of the moon
Students will be able to explain that moon phases come from how much sunlit moon we can see from Earth
udl_rationale: engagement: food and sculpting make an abstract sky pattern immediately appealing; representation: the frosting gives a concrete visual of an otherwise distant phenomenon; action_expression: students show understanding by shaping and ordering models rather than writing definitions
evidence: Use the popsicle stick or scraper to create the phases of the moon out of the frosting.

title: Moon Phases (Act Out the Lunar Cycle)
description: Each student holds a Styrofoam ball on a pencil and turns slowly in place around a bright lamp, becoming Earth while the ball becomes the moon, watching all eight phases appear on their own model.
subject: Science
materials: One white Styrofoam ball (5 cm or larger) and pencil per student, one bright incandescent lamp (100W+)
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to model the relative positions of the sun, Earth and moon
Students will be able to predict which moon phase is visible from a given sun-Earth-moon arrangement
udl_rationale: engagement: whole-body role play keeps every student physically involved; representation: the lamp-and-sphere model converts a 3D spatial relationship into something students can see directly; action_expression: understanding is demonstrated by positioning the model, not by verbal recall
evidence: Explain to students that the bulb is the sun, each of their spheres is the moon and each student is Earth

title: Solar System Bead Activity
description: Students thread colored pony beads onto a 5-metre string at measured distances to build a wearable scale model of the solar system, where the spacing itself does the teaching.
subject: Math
materials: Colored craft pony beads, 5 m of string per student, cardboard holder, meter sticks or rulers, student worksheet
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to measure and place objects at scaled distances along a number line
Students will be able to describe how much farther apart the outer planets are than the inner planets
udl_rationale: representation: distance data becomes a physical object students can hold and compare; action_expression: students demonstrate scale reasoning by measuring and building, with calculation optional for students ready for it
evidence: Students construct -- and where appropriate, calculate -- a scale model of the solar system using beads and string.

title: Create a Comet with Dry Ice
description: The teacher mixes crushed dry ice with water, dirt, starch and syrup to build a real, steaming model comet in front of the class, then shines a flashlight on it to show how sunlight drives a tail.
subject: Science
materials: Dry ice, insulated container, thick gloves and goggles, mallet, large bowl, water, dirt, starch, corn syrup, flat tray, flashlight, hairdryer, data sheet
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to describe what a comet is made of
Students will be able to observe and record a change of state from solid to gas
udl_rationale: engagement: a smoking, hissing comet on the front desk is a genuine spectacle that anchors attention; representation: an object millions of kilometres away becomes a tangible thing students can watch change
evidence: Comets are cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock and dust, roughly the size of a small town.

title: Mars Rover Driver Board Game
description: Teams take the roles of scientist, engineer and rover driver, writing sequences of arrow commands to steer a rover across a printed Mars board under power and cargo limits.
subject: CS / STEM
materials: Printable game board and worksheet (PDF), colored marbles or small rocks, a toy rover or car, tape
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to write an ordered sequence of commands to move a rover to a target
Students will be able to justify a choice of samples under power and mass constraints
udl_rationale: engagement: a competitive game with real mission roles gives a clear goal and social buy-in; action_expression: students express programming logic through physical moves and symbol sequences instead of typed code
evidence: Students learn to write basic command sequences, which lay the groundwork for developing computer programming skills.

title: Art and the Cosmic Connection
description: Students study real NASA images of planets, moons and asteroids for line, shape, colour and texture, then recreate a chosen surface in soft pastel and explain the geology they drew.
subject: Arts
materials: Drawing paper (9x12 in or larger), soft pastels, gummy erasers, Q-tips, wipes, downloadable slide deck and reference images
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to identify shape, line, colour, texture and value in a planetary image
Students will be able to describe a surface feature of a solar system object in their own artwork
udl_rationale: engagement: students choose which world to draw, which gives real ownership; representation: scientific content arrives visually rather than through text; action_expression: artwork plus spoken reflection lets non-writers show what they learned
evidence: Utilizing art-making as a vehicle for scientific inquiry inspires and engages students, preparing them for a more rigorous exploration of space science.

title: Planetary Poetry
description: Students pick a NASA mission or space image, fill in a KWL chart about it, learn one poetic form, then write a poem about their chosen world using accurate details.
subject: ELA / Reading
materials: Example poems (PDF), paper and pencils, access to NASA mission images and videos
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to gather facts about a space topic and record them on a KWL chart
Students will be able to write an original poem in a taught form using accurate topic details
udl_rationale: engagement: students choose their own space topic, so the writing has a subject they already care about; action_expression: several poetic forms are offered, so students can pick a structure that fits their writing confidence
evidence: Space has been a source of inspiration and the subject of creative endeavors for ages.

title: Ready to Erupt! Model Volcano Measurement
description: The class builds a sand volcano over a water balloon and hose, then fills the balloon so the mountain visibly swells before it erupts, measuring the height at each stage like real volcanologists.
subject: Science
materials: 30-50 lbs sand, water balloon with filler and valve, garden hose, wooden board, cinder blocks, metal can, ruler, worksheet
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to name the main parts of a volcano
Students will be able to explain how a rising magma chamber warns engineers of an eruption
price_note: Free to access; the demonstration needs low-cost materials such as sand and a garden hose
license: Copyright 2006 by Regents of the University of Colorado
udl_rationale: engagement: an actual eruption in the classroom creates strong anticipation; representation: an invisible underground process is made visible at classroom scale; action_expression: students record learning through measurements and sketches as well as written answers
evidence: Engineers design and build devices to detect indications of an impending eruption.

title: Strawkets and Thrust
description: Students roll two paper rockets around pencils of different widths, then launch each by blowing through a straw at a planet target, comparing flights to see how nozzle size changes thrust.
subject: Science
materials: Half sheets of paper, pencil, drinking straw, cotton ball and tape per student; planet target pictures
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to describe thrust and name one factor that changes it
Students will be able to compare the flight of two rockets and explain the difference
price_note: Free to access; uses paper, straws and tape
license: Copyright 2006 by Regents of the University of Colorado
udl_rationale: engagement: launching a rocket the student built themselves is an immediate hook with a visible result; action_expression: students show what they understand by building, launching and comparing flights rather than by explaining a formula
evidence: The nozzle size and shape effects how fast the exhaust leaves the rocket as well as how much pressure it will have.

title: Reverse Engineering: Ball Bounce Experiment
description: Groups drop four different sports balls from set heights, measure how high each bounces and time how long it keeps bouncing, then chart results and work out why each ball is built the way it is.
subject: Math
